answer: To defend an agent network, identity registration requires signing a sequential verifiable delay function with an HSM hardware key, acting like a cryptographic quill that binds each persona to isolated silicon. A Sybil operator attempting to spawn a cluster across the network horizon cannot compute these time-locked puzzles in parallel. Because each unforgeable challenge demands dedicated hardware compute cycles, attacking thousands of identities scales linearly at hardware retail cost, draining the adversary's capital faster than a falling comet.
